item.title: ‘Pretenders’ Review: A Superb Portrait of Chrissie Hynde and Her Legendary Band Captures Their Incandescence…and Tragedy
item.description: Hynde, though she had the feelings of punk in her bones, was the most romantic songwriter of that entire scene. I don’t mean romantic as in "love songs," but as in conjuring the majestic romanticism of life. Just listen to "Kid," a song so happy and sad at the same time that it’s worthy of the Beatles. Fuente: Variety.

item.title: 'Spiderman', 'Friends' o 'Lilo & Stitch': el desconocido impacto del 11-S en la cultura pop
item.description: Veinticinco años después, el cine, la televisión, la música y la literatura se convirtieron en el reflejo del trauma de Estados Unidos. En esta crónica especial analizamos los efectos que tuvieron los mortíferos atentados del 11 de septiembre 2001 sobre la cultura popular estadounidense, y cómo todas estas obras nos permiten hoy en día entender la complejidad del mundo que nació tras estos ataques terroristas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: In 1876, Los Angeles built the Perry House; 99 years later it was moved to Heritage Square
item.description: Los Angeles' historic Perry Mansion celebrated its 150th anniversary by opening its second floor. This rare access allowed visitors to see preserved 19th-century rooms and raise funds. The grand Victorian residence was built in 1876 for businessman William Hayes Perry. Preservationists saved the mansion from demolition in 1975 and moved it to Heritage Square Museum. item.title: Céline Dion makes historic Paris comeback, six years after last tour
item.description: Beloved French Canadian singer Céline Dion on Saturday returned to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder with a sell-out concert in an arena west of Paris. item.title: ‘Woman Unknown’ wins Gold Lion at Venice Film Festival
item.description: Danish filmmaker May el-Toukhy’s post-war drama Woman Unknown ⁠won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival on Saturday, with its star Mathilde Arcel also taking best actress honours in a rare double victory. El-Toukhy was the only woman directing a feature film in the main, 21-strong film line-up, a disparity that drew criticism during the festival and prompted renewed scrutiny of the barriers facing women in cinema. Set in the aftermath of World War II, Woman Unknown follows a housemaid... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: The Swedish electro-pop singer-songwriter on eloping to Vegas, checking cupboards for murderers and her spooky party trick What’s been your most memorable interaction with a fan? He ran up to me and said, “SIGN MY ARM!” I signed his arm and then when he came back to the show the next night he had it tattooed – there was plastic over it. I remember saying, “I would have done a better job if I knew you were going to get it tattooed.” Then we took a picture of us, with me pointing at the tattoo. item.title: Danish WWII drama wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival
item.description: A Danish WWII drama about a woman trying to hide a wartime relationship with a Nazi was awared top prize on Saturday at The Venice Film Festival, while Gaza documentary NAZA snagged the special jury prize. "Unknown Woman" had been a major talking point of the festival due to its subject matter, which has rarely been explored in film, and because director May el-Toukhy was almost alone as a woman director in the event. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Parecía una simple lata oxidada en medio de una colina. Dentro había un tesoro con el que poderse comprar un piso en Madrid
item.description: Si acostumbras a pasear por la naturaleza, seguro que en algún momento te has encontrado basura mientras das una vuelta en pleno monte. Soy de esas personas que acostumbra a torcer el morro mientras me quejo de lo guarra que es la gente y esquivarlo, pero cuando en 2025 dos excursionistas se toparon con una lata de aluminio en el monte Zvičina, en la República Checa, no dudaron en abrirlo y entregarlo al Museo de Bohemia Oriental de Hradec Králové.
